title: November 5 — vines, borrowed support and procedural garden worlds
summary: Three distinct implementations turn local growth and external support into an evolutionary test, a playable load-bearing garden and a room-based visual game. Emergence3DSol inherits the supplied 3D ecology and adds support-grip interventions; Koynnos models growing tips, chains/pins, load-responsive fig roots and a writable crystal field; PsychedelicGarden extends the AnttisBrain2 Descent room engine with vine-caged keys and motion-fed growth. They share imagery and causal questions but not proven learning or common code.

nodes.claim: Controlled extension of Emergence3D's fixed-transformer, heritable-genome voxel ecology. Adds inert vertical rods, rod/foreign-body proximity sensing, selectable grip that discounts synthetic altitude stress, inherited phase-guided horizontal search and rod-severing interventions.
nodes.survived: Implements matched four-arm vine/grip-without-twine/no-grip/no-rods comparisons, a sever-at step intervention, grip and high-cell occupancy diagnostics, save/load, and source-reported CPU integration tests. Rod shading and physical obstruction are held constant across the three primary adhesion comparisons.
nodes.killed: No committed multi-seed outcome in README demonstrates evolutionary benefit from gripping or twining. Circumnutation and attachment incentives are designed into the world; support is an energy discount, not simulated forces, weight-bearing chains, learned network weights or independently evolved biological strategy.
nodes.era: November 5: growth, borrowed support and interactive worlds

nodes.claim: A Three.js browser garden with sweeping vine probes, attached growth, shared hanging chains with cumulative pin loads, fig-like descending roots that may unload pins, woody vine-on-vine supports, and a writable 2D crystal field underneath a 3D scene.
nodes.survived: Playable published WebGL instrument with controls for planting vines and figs, hanging chains, crystal events, following a growing tip, altering growth rules, observing pin load bars, and seeded replay through URL fragments. Implements support dependency and local-versus-shared cost as observable toy rules.
nodes.killed: No controlled, multi-seed evidence that circumnutation, root rescue or growing on other vines is adaptively advantageous. The pin/chain physics and writable crystal field are stylized; the system is neither trained AI nor a biological, mechanical or evolutionary validation.
nodes.era: November 5: growth, borrowed support and interactive worlds

nodes.claim: Browser WebGL2 raymarched game built from the AnttisBrain2 Descent engine's hashed rooms, mirror moons and webcam-reactive boundaries. Chains suspend moons; analytic SDF vines grow toward them; room-level motion advances a vine cage guarding the key moon and opens the exit seal.
nodes.survived: Repository describes a complete key/cage/gate/next-room gameplay loop with WASD, vertical flight, webcam-or-navigation growth input and SDF-rendered chained moons. README reports a headless shader-compile and game-logic test.
nodes.killed: No measured real-GPU frame rate, player usability or long-run game performance. Reported headless checks do not establish interactive browser performance; growth is an authored game mechanic, not evolved biological or AI learning.
nodes.era: November 5: growth, borrowed support and interactive worlds

edges.why: Emergence3DSol explicitly identifies itself as a controlled extension of the Emergence3D voxel world and preserves the prior genome/ecology loop while adding rods, contact sensing, support and controls.

Koynnos explicitly cites Emergence3DSol as a related but independent implementation: both examine support-seeking vine growth, but only Emergence3DSol frames inherited selection and quantitative ablations.

Koynnos explicitly cites PsychedelicGarden as related in spirit; both stage vines and chains in interactive 3D scenes, but one is a key-and-gate raymarched game and the other a support/load toy garden.

motifs.title: Local contact can help one tip while accumulating cost elsewhere
motifs.description: Grip in Emergence3DSol discounts a local synthetic stress; Koynnos makes the shared chain pin and its capacity visible, with rescue by grounded fig roots. The two are distinct representations of dependency and need intervention controls before transferring conclusions.

motifs.title: Growth can be an ecological hypothesis, a readable instrument or a game gate
motifs.description: One branch tests an evolutionary support advantage, one offers interactive chain/vine exploration, and one turns motion into rule-governed progression through procedural rooms. Similar 3D plant imagery is not evidence of the same solver or learned algorithm.
